claims.claim: the test suite is 97 tests and they pass
claims.probe: test $(PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q 2>&1 | grep -oE 'Ran [0-9]+ tests' | grep -oE '[0-9]+') -ge 97

claims.claim: the gate is shadow-mode and blocks nothing; a would-DENY is recorded, not enforced
claims.where: README.md How it gets in the middle + ANSWERS.md Rules and policy

claims.claim: ingest is idempotent — a cursor-advanced re-fetch of the same source yields nothing
claims._note: was './bin/paymaster ingest && ./bin/paymaster ingest | grep ...', which MUTATED the real ledger and auto-committed anchor commits every time reconcile ran, and was racy against live telemetry arriving between the two calls. A probe must observe the claim, not perform it.

claims.claim: x402 adapter matches vendored spec v2
reconcile detects and overwrites corrupt counter cache
MCP server exposes exactly ingest/check/report/consider/coverage/verify/explain/reconcile_counters, and never grant/revoke-cap/enroll/x402
claims.probe: for t in ingest check report consider coverage verify explain reconcile_counters; do grep -q "def $t" mcp_server/server.py || exit 1; done && ! grep -qE 'def (grant|revoke_cap|enroll|x402)' mcp_server/server.py

claims.claim: mcp_server/server.py is syntactically valid and the advertised test quickstart works on a fresh clone with no local state
claims.probe: python3 -m py_compile mcp_server/server.py && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q

claims.claim: ORIGIN.md, AUTHORS.md, CHANGELOG.md exist and README links all three
claims.probe: test -f ORIGIN.md && test -f AUTHORS.md && test -f CHANGELOG.md && rg -q 'ORIGIN.md' README.md && rg -q 'CHANGELOG.md' README.md && rg -q 'AUTHORS.md' README.md

claims.claim: license sign/verify/activate roundtrip works, rejects tampered/garbage/forged keys, and verification needs only the public key (not the private signing key)
when enforcement is enabled, ingest/check block once the trial cap is exceeded and no license is active; report/verify/explain stay ungated
claims.probe: grep -q 'TRIAL_GATED = {"ingest", "check"}' bin/paymaster && grep -q 'cmd in TRIAL_GATED and L.enforcement_enabled()' bin/paymaster

claims.claim: license enforcement ships dormant — nothing is gated unless PAYMASTER_LICENSE=1 is set
claims.probe: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest tests.test_license.TestEnforcementIsDormantByDefault -q && PYTHONPATH=src ./bin/paymaster license status | grep -q 'enforcement: DORMANT'

claims.claim: without the cryptography package the gate fails open rather than locking out a paid user, and activate blames the missing package instead of the key
issue-license is operator-only — not reachable via bin/paymaster dispatch or the MCP server
